version.changelog: v1.1.5 — The Transparency Update: Added Security Scanners & False Positives section explaining why VirusTotal/Zenbox flag defensive behaviors. Zero behavior changes.

llm.summary: The skill's code and documentation are broadly consistent with a pre-install sandboxing tool, but important runtime orchestration pieces were truncated from the review and several behaviors (local Docker image build, optional root-requiring micro-VM mode, eBPF tracing) increase risk and deserve manual review before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (pre-install sandboxing) match the included artifacts: obfuscator, entropy gate, behavioral auditor, output filter, orchestrator, and a Dockerfile. Requested binaries (docker, python3) and no environment variables are proportionate to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs building a local Docker runner and running a deterministic pipeline that extracts a transcript, obfuscates code, runs it in an isolated runtime, collects traces, and filters outputs. These instructions reasonably map to the declared purpose. However the runtime orchestration (microvm_orchestrator, eBPF trace collection, transcript_extractor) is critical to security and several of those files were truncated in the provided bundle; you should verify they do not mount host paths writable, do not send data to external endpoints, and enforce network=none/seccomp as documented.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No formal install spec (instruction-only) lowers risk, but SKILL.md directs building a Docker image that pulls a distroless base (gcr.io) at build time. That pull is expected but will require network access. The build is local (no third-party download URL), which is appropriate; still verify the included Dockerfile and builder stage behavior before running.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The code uses the Docker binary path and copies os.environ into subprocesses, but it does not declare or require secrets. This is proportionate to the stated function. Do note the orchestrator passes the calling environment to subprocesses, so avoid running it in an environment that has sensitive variables set.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and allows user invocation. It documents an optional Firecracker micro-VM mode that requires root/KVM access; that is consistent with providing stronger isolation but increases privilege needs. Confirm the micro-VM path is optional and that Docker/container mode operates without elevated host privileges and with read-only mounts and seccomp as described.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package largely does what it says: it obfuscates and runs untrusted features in a container/VM, audits syscalls and entropy, and sanitizes outputs. Before running it in your environment: 1) Inspect microvm_orchestrator.py, transcript_extractor.py, and any truncated files to ensure they do not perform network calls, write to sensitive host paths, or leak data. 2) Build and run the runner image in an isolated machine or throwaway VM (so docker pulls and container execution cannot access secrets on your workstation). 3) Verify mounts are read-only and --network=none and that the provided seccomp profile is actually applied. 4) Do not run the optional Firecracker/KVM path on a production host unless you understand and consent to root-level operations. 5) Keep secrets out of your shell environment when invoking the orchestrator (it passes os.environ into subprocesses). If you want higher assurance, run the code review or tests inside a dedicated ephemeral VM and/or request the full, untruncated source for an independent review.
